data.title: Repair and Rehabilitation of WASH Facilities in Households in Jordan
data.description: Syrian Refugees have been fleeing the devastating impact of the Syrian Civil War since 2011, however with the increase in reporting and border closures the impact of the mass migration is being felt throughout Europe and neighbouring Countries. Oxfam have identified the needs of Syrian refugees fleeing to Jordan and have designed a water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) project to support these needs. This includes supporting Syrian refugees and vulnerable Jordanian households with WASH support in the form of repairs and rehabilitation.

data.title: Combating Sexual and Gender-Based Violence to retain girls and boys in Malawian schools for improved
data.description: This project aims to tackle the prevalence of School Based Sexual Violence in schools. It will work with pupils, schools staff and communities to raise awareness and build effective and functional mechanisms to report and deal with any. There will be a primary focus on girls but boys are clearly integral to this work through their involvement and the ability and relevance of the mechanisms to support any incidences of sexual abuse against boys and young men. The mechanisms created will ensure that both communities and schools remain safe places for young people to grow up and develop in. Working with two experienced local organisations, Oxfam Malawi will be part of an effective partnership.

data.title: QuidsIn
data.description: QuidsIn is a digital payment card for people on low incomes that incorporates an emergency savings fund. Users have a prepayment card that is used for everyday shopping. Members save small amounts as they shop and this saving is matched by corporate/statutory partners. Members redeem their savings when they experience financial shock.

data.description: This project will work with 500 women seeking sanctuary in Cardiff, Swansea, Newport and Wrexham over a three year period. The aim of this project is to better enable refugees, asylum seekers and failed asylum seekers to integrate into the by increased employment and training opportunities, social inclusion and community involvement activities, and engagement which will improve services in the future. These activities will provide a holistic approach to meet the differing needs of beneficiaries.

data.title: Roars not Whispers
data.description: Roars not Whispers is a 3-year youth led programme that will build the capacity of young people to represent themselves and others, take action on issues of concern and bring these issues further up the public and political agenda in Scotland. Oxfam and the Scottish Youth Parliament will deliver the work with a wide range of other youth focused groups involved. Young people from every local authority area in Scotland will be trained as peer educators.

data.title: Refugee and Asylum Seeking Women in Wales
data.description: This project will work in partnership with Refugee Community Organisations (grass roots refugee and asylum seeker organisations) in Swansea, Newport and Cardiff to address the particular issues faced by refugee and asylum seeking women. This will include provision of drop-ins and activities to reduce social isolation. It will provide training to women to become champions for their community and advocates for better services to meet the specific needs of the target beneficiaries.

data.title: The VCS Emergency Partnerships (VCSEP) coordination of the local COVID-19 response
data.description: The British Red Cross is already subsidising the costs of the VCSEP with its own funding, and will continue to do so alongside Government grant funding. A contribution of 200,000 from DCMS is critical in enabling the VCSEP to scale up its response to the COVID-19 pandemic, providing vital coordination and support to a wider network of charities and communities on the ground. By funding dedicated staff time, we enable the VCSEP staff to focus on delivery of the VCSEPs COVID-19 coordination only, rather than delivering this in a part time capacity alongside their regular charity (British Red Cross and others) work. This will facilitate a much more effective and efficient response which is necessary in the face of a fast-moving emergency.

data.description: The programme aims to increase sustainable and shared prosperity in Kenya by increasing Kenyas trade with the region and the rest of the world. Specifically, the programme will (i) invest in improving the efficiency and capacity of transport, logistics and trade infrastructure at Mombasa Port and key border points; (ii) invest in systems to improve trading standards, reduce non-tariff barriers and enhance transparency in trade processes; (iii) improve the regulatory and policy environment for trade; and (iv) support private sector advocacy for trade competitiveness, the export capacity of Kenyan businesses and the greater participation of women and small and growing businesses in trade. ICF component is supporting Kenya Ports Authority to develop and implement a Green Port Policy to help the port adapt and become resilient to climate change. Key objectives include introducing new climate friendly technologies into the ports operations.

data.title: Family Reunion
data.description: The right to family life and Family Reunification is a fundamental part of international law. Families have been separated through conflict and persecution and in the current refugee crisis has seen a sharp increase in this as often only one family member can afford to seek sanctuary. Changes to the immigration act and the eventual implementation of Brexit could also see a rise in families being separated. Comic Relief has previously worked with British Red Cross on the ground-breaking “not so straightforward” report to demonstrate the difficulties of family reunion and importantly to reunite families here in the UK. This grant carries on that work in a consortium with other funders. The new iteration of the work ‘Families Together’ will see a collective approach to supporting family reunion, with BRC and smaller grassroots charities working together to improve access and reunite more families. This programme will test different models of delivery, partnership working, strategic litigation, awareness raising and improving policy and access to advice and ultimately help reunite families who have been torn apart.

recipientOrganization.name: British Red Cross
recipientOrganization.description: The British Red Cross plays a vital role in emergency response. In times of crisis, we’re here to help people. We’re local and we’re global and we’ve been doing this for 150 years. Our network of incredible staff and volunteers means we are uniquely placed to reach people in fearful, uncertain times. Our vision is a world where everyone gets the help they need in a crisis. Our mission is to mobilise the power of humanity so that individuals have the capacity to prepare for, deal with and recover from crisis. More and more people are finding themselves in vulnerable situations. Those most at risk include people who are displaced, people with overlapping health conditions, the fail and older people. We want to ensure that people and communities experiencing the greatest health inequalities have fair and equitable access to the right care, at the right time. We are working to make sure fewer people use emergency healthcare services or get stuck in hospital due to lack of support to live safely at home.

recipientOrganization.name: British Red Cross
recipientOrganization.description: First Call - run by the British Red Cross in Northamptonshire - provides a vital lifeline to local people who are suffering a loss of independence as a result of a personal crisis - for example recovering from an operation, illness or accident. Put simply, it allows people to get better better. Too many people are stuck in hospital who would be able to return home if only they had some support during their recovery period. Our First Call service provides that support, it prevents hospital re-admissions and, crucially, allows people to recover more quickly. The support package is individual, it can include light cleaning, shopping and other practical tasks; not everyone has the same needs and the aim of the service is to agree goals with our clients and then support them in achieving those goals. We also know that companionship during this time can be equally important as a loss of independence is often very isolating. Typically, our volunteers work with service users over a 12 week period to help them establish links to their community and statutory agencies, so that once the First call service comes to an end the client has an on going network of support. This service is delivered locally, co-ordinated locally, managed and directed locally. Everyone involved with this service, from volunteers to managers, are from and operates in the Northamptonshire area. This service is very specific to the Northamptonshire area - it is not provided in this form elsewhere. It is also fundraised for locally, by Nothamptonshire volunteers, a Northamptonshire Area President (Lady Elwood) and Northamptonshire Area Volunteer Committee (with the assistance of the area's Senior Community Fundraiser).

data.description: As directed by the donor towards the work of the British Red Cross. The British Red Cross helps people in crisis, whoever and wherever they are. We are part of a global network of volunteers, responding to natural disasters, conflicts and individual emergencies. We enable vulnerable people at home and overseas to prepare for and respond to emergencies in their own communities. And when the crisis is over, we help people to recover and move on with their lives.

recipientOrganization.name: British Red Cross
recipientOrganization.description: Our mission at the British Red Cross is to mobilise the power of humanity so that individuals have the capacity to prepare for, deal with and recover from crisis. Since 1870 we have been helping people who need it most, no matter who or where they are. In the UK we provide patient transport and at home support alongside the NHS and other partners, offer lifesaving First Aid training, aid in community resilience and crisis response alongside the emergency services and are a major provider of refugee and asylum seeker support. Our current UK strategy focuses on three areas we believe we can make the most difference: disasters and emergencies, health inequalities, and displacement and migration. By 2030 we aim to ensure people are safe and able to survive and recover whenever disaster strikes, that people in the UK receive the care and support they need without falling through gaps in the health system and that people experiencing displacement feel safe, live with dignity and have choice and opportunity on their journey.

data.title: Supporting Refugees and Asylum Seekers to Survive and Thrive in Derby
data.description: The British Red Cross will support recently arrived refugees and asylum seekers to help them recover from crisis, improve their standard of living, reduce isolation and improve their health and well-being. It will work with Upbeat Communities and the Multi-Faith Centre to help individuals and families to adapt to their new environment. Immediate support will include emergency supplies and then additional support for up to two years.

data.title: Supporting refugees, asylum seekers and migrants in Luton and Essex
data.description: This is the expansion of a project supporting refugees and asylum seekers in Luton and Essex. Alongside support with immediate basic needs such as sleeping bags, food parcels and temporary accommodation, people will be offered social activities, peer support, volunteering opportunities, help with applying for support from local authorities and familiarisation tours of the local area. The group will work with the local community and media to promote positive messages about refugees and asylum seekers.

data.title: Tees Valley Ariadne - Refugee and Asylum Support Partnership
data.description: This new project will provide support for refugees and asylum seekers in Middlesbrough, Stockton and Hartlepool to help them find a way out of destitution, achieve integration and make a contribution to the local community. New arrivals will receive orientation and information about key local services including doctors, schools, hospitals, wellbeing courses to reduce anxiety and social drop-ins to make friends and connect locally.

data.description: Working with Citizens Advice Reading and Oxford City of Sanctuary the project will support refugees, asylum seekers and vulnerable migrants. data.title: Providing education to refugee and displaced children and youth in South Sudan and Ethiopia
data.description: As a result of the continuing conflict in South Sudan, large numbers of people have moved east towards the border with Ethiopia. Children and young people, many already traumatized, face the risk of further violence and conscription into local militias. But the continuing conflict means that primary schools have closed and teachers are not paid. In the refugee camps in Ethiopia local authorities are over-stretched and there is as yet no funding provision from the Government for the education of refugees. This proposal will enable refugee children on both sides of the border to receive a basic education, for one year, with an emphasis on providing protection and improving their life skills.

data.title: Tuwekeze Pamoja: Working together to give children in Tanzania a better start to life
data.description: For a child growing up in rural Tanzania the chance of staying in school and achieving the grades needed to go to secondary school is low. This project aims to give children from birth to age 6 the best possible start to life by working with parents, schools, communities and government to promote a safe and conducive environment for learning - at home and school. There is a large investment in research to understand what inputs at this early age really make a difference, with an opportunity to influence government policy and wider practice in early childhood development. As a result of the project, children will be able to thrive and fulfil their potential.

data.title: Family Grants Programme
data.description: Save the Children?s Family Grants Programme is a strategic tool to combat the lifelong impact of poverty. It delivers crucial financial support to families in crisis. Intervention at critical moments of vulnerability, such as a sudden change in circumstance like job loss or housing instability, to the unexpected cost of a household appliance. The grant provides £300 to families in crisis, for essentials like cots, carpets, or shoes. This is via a network of 120 trusted Referral Partners such as HomeStart centres, Children?s Centres, Citizens Advice, Primary schools and GPs. This ensures support reaches those most in need. The Family Grants Programme Eligibility requirement · Have at least one child under 18; or be 28 or more weeks pregnant · Meet the low-income threshold, evidenced by being in receipt of, or applying for at least one benefit; and/or · Be experiencing financial hardship that is pushing them into poverty, despite being in work Overall the grant programme aims to distribute nearly £1.6m over three years with 4660 grants supporting an estimated 17,000 people

data.title: #Digital7 Queer Heritage and Collections Network
data.description: Having done some initial testing we plan to roll out a digital programme of training and workshops, publicly-accessible online presentations of LGBTQ+ heritage research, virtual sessions for members to evaluateand develop their public engagement, and pilot community-lead online intervention activities to identify new connections to queer heritage in five member museums through 'tag-athons' and facilitate creative online access to these objects and narratives during the 'create-athons'. To achieve this, we will identify the collections and their needs; work with staff, volunteers and community partners to explore and identify the desired digitaloutputs for their collections and audiences; and bring together this digital content, a crowdsourced toolkit and other resources in one online hub.

data.title: Heart of the Dales
data.description: The Heart of the Dales Landscape Recovery project covers over 9,000ha of the Yorkshire Dales, improving water quality by reducing runoff and erosion, adding buffers and looking for opportunities for naturalisation, putting more trees into the landscape, improving biodiversity through increased habitat connectivity, structure, quality and diversity and helping our farmers adapt to climate change. This will involve a mix of appropriate regenerative grazing regimes, no inputs, habitat protection and restoration, tree establishment, peat restoration and creation of new habitat such as woodlands, hay meadows, species rich grasslands and wood pasture.

fundingOrganization.name: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

recipientOrganization.name: The National Trust for Places of Historic Interest or Natural Beauty

data.title: High Peak Nature Recovery
data.description: High Peak Nature Recovery will be a paradigm shift in how we manage 9,681Ha of our land in the PeakDistrict to help tackle the nature and climate crisis. In partnership with tenant farmers, we will workholistically to restore natural processes through changes to grazing practises whilst supporting theirbusinesses to thrive. A large programme of capital works will restore >5,000Ha of peatlands and create>2000Ha of wooded habitats, establishing a mosaic of habitats which store carbon and support anabundance of wildlife. We will also protect and restore species rich habitats and significant heritageassets for everyone, forever

data.title: CCC 056-CF2552
data.description: Seeking to enhance and progress coordination for coastal sustainability and resilience in England. The 3Cs initiative will use this funding to: Test, trial and inform best practice approaches for coastal coordination in England. The overall ambition is for a strengthened and well supported national framework covering the entire English coast to integrate place-based delivery for coastal ecosystems and communities. Determine how the existing activities of those involved on coastal governance can be strengthened to better coordinate and achieve improvements to coastal environments that are linked to enhanced social and economic outcomes, and how governance systems can be capacitated to facilitate this process. Explore how to make better use of resources, share ownership of complex issues and maximise outcomes through a collaborative approach of organisations from the public sector, private sector. Defra sub-outcome: 1.5 Improved access to nature

data.description: This measure covers grants for investments in forest area development and improvement of the viability of forests under Countryside Productivity and ESIF Growth Programme.Forest areas supported under this Measure must be managed in accordance with the UKFS. All holdings over 10 ha must have an approved woodland management plan in place. The measure supports investments in modernising forestry technologies; improving resilience, environmental value and mitigation potential of forest ecosystems; achieving nature, biodiversity and wider ecosystem services objectives; adapting to climate change; forest protection; and creating new woodland and forested areas (except short rotation coppice, Christmas trees and fast growing trees for energy production).State or publicly owned land is not eligible for maintenance payments even if the holder is a private body or individual.RPA administers for measures in England.

data.title: State Aid Funded (Measure 16)
data.description: This measure covers grants for Co-operation under Countryside Productivity, Countryside Stewardship and ESIF Growth Programme to micro and small enterprises, farmers and foresters engaged in cooperative activities.This measure encourages and promotes a range of cooperative activity which encourages farmers, forest holders, private businesses and public bodies, or participants in supply chains to work together to take forward priorities for investment and overcome disadvantages of fragmentation.The measure develops priorities in environment, climate change and biodiversity; supporting farmers and foresters to improve supply chains or develop short supply chains; develop initiatives to tackle animal health and welfare issues; as well as cooperation between public bodies and private businesses to develop the rural economy.Local co-operation in tourism activities are supported that improve the attractiveness of the overall destination, help develop the supply chain in the visitor economy and encourage collaborative activity or pilot projects developing agri-food hubs or clusters in particular geographic areas. This measure will be used to implement the European Innovation Partnership for agricultural productivity and sustainability.RPA administers for measures in England

data.description: This covers grants made for investments in physical assets made under Countryside Stewardship.The measure supports various farm and forestry investments in particular for businesses investing in innovative business practices and new technologies to make them more sustainable and productive. data.title: EAFRD - RD Measure 10
data.description: This measure covers Agri-environment-organic farming support.Payments are based on income foregone and, where relevant, additional costs resulting from converting to an organic farming system. There are 5 different conversion payments available for different farming systems: Rotational Land; Improved Permanent Pasture; Unimproved Permanent Pasture; Horticulture; and Top Fruit.This measure aims to fund organic conversion and maintenance by active farmers and builds on existing conversion and maintenance support under the previous RD programme Environmental Stewardship (Organic Higher Level and Entry Level Stewardship) elements.Activities funded under this measure support farmers wishing to convert to and maintain organic farming systems for environmental benefits. Investments contribute to meeting Englands Biodiversity 2020 goals and legal obligations under the Habitats and Species and Water Framework Directives. Support also aims to deliver the main objectives on biodiversity and the water environment (including flood management).RPA administers for measures in England.

data.title: National Trust, Landing Steps and Bridge to the south of Spring Lodge, Taplow
data.description: The proposed work for which funding is requested is for enabling works to allow the steps, landing and balustrade to be surveyed and assessed, so the extent, (and cost), of the repairs can be identified. This would include an inspection to be undertaken in line with HEAG099 - Understanding Historic Buildings - Level 2, to provide electronic survey drawings, a photographic schedule and a condition survey, providing the information required which will enable the scope and nature of the repair work which is necessary to be fully understood and developed. The funding would also allow for materials analysis to be undertaken, including mortar and stone sampling, testing for deleterious materials, drains surveys and testing, and ecological surveys to be completed, all informing the repair work which is necessary.

recipientOrganization.description: The National Trust is the largest conservation charity in Europe, entirely independent of Government. It was founded in 1895 by three people who wanted to bring people closer to nature, beauty and history. The National Trust spends over £150 million a year on conservation projects that help look after more than 250,000 hectares of countryside and 780 miles of coastline, including forests, woods, fens, beaches and farmland, plus over 500 historic properties, including houses, castles, nature reserves, gardens, ancient monuments and archaeological remains. The National Trust is for everyone, and it was founded for the benefit of the whole nation. We receive on average more than 26.9 million visits each year to places with an entry fee, and an estimated 100 million visits to outdoor places that are free of charge. Paying visitors, over 5.6 million members and more than 46,000 volunteers support our work.

data.description: The award will fund coordination a project to encourage BME groups to explore the rich heritage that surrounds the Sutton Hall property. A trail called The History of Black Londoners will be established, alongside a range of music and story telling events held at Sutton House. The project will be directly linked to De Beavoiur School, Hackney.

data.title: The NATHAN Project
data.description: Biomass heating systems will be installed at twelve National Trust properties. The systems will reduce annual carbon emissions by 1200 tonnes and provide opportunities to show the technology to 1.5 million annual visitors to these sites.

data.title: Getting into the past - new futures for young people
data.description: This project is to fund a vocational experience for disadvantaged young people. The project will be split into a three tiers, which are the processes that the young people would go through. Firstly the young people will be involved in 'Team' which is a 12 week community project consisting of residentials and team building exercises. The second stage will be the involvement of young people into the 'Get Into' which is a two week taster session on a National Trust site in an area of interest of them.

data.title: Family Places
data.description: This project will take place at various National Trust properties across Devon and Cornwall. Activities will include photography, growing and cooking food and green gardening. They will focus on building confidence and enjoyment of learning together, and will develop literacy and numeracy skills where possible. The project will deliver 30 activities per year with an average of 14 participants. Twenty will take place at National Trust properties and 10 outreach activities will take place each year.

data.title: 'The Bower' project at Sheringham Park
data.description: The project will transform a former car park, in Sheringham Park, into a multi-purpose wildlife area. The group will install a perimeter fence to exclude dogs, create a new path around the perimeter of the area for dog walkers, provide a bird feeding station and install CCTV for wildlife observation. A hazel-coppice entrance gate will be created a sensory trail planted with species selected for the way they feel, sound and smell. A meeting area, seating and picnic tables will also be provided.

data.title: The 'Wicked' Woodland Adventure Project
data.description: This project based in the grounds of Sudbury Hall, Derbyshire will develop a free access woodland play area for local and visiting children.  It will also deliver mobile outreach play activities to children living in rurally isolated communities surrounding Sudbury Hall, which also houses the Museum of Childhood. The project aims to benefit over 26,000 children and young people over two years.

data.title: A View of the Mount
data.description: This heritage group work with the National Trust to manage a historic site which contains an old windmill. They will purchase and install interpretation boards in the windmill and commission a scale model of the castle which once stood nearby.

data.title: #Coed2 Adfer Coetir Hynafol Ysbyty (ACHY) / Ysbyty Ancient Woodland Restoration
data.description:
Our vision is ‘accessible healthy woodlands at the heart of community life’. 

The project will open-up previously inaccessible woodlands on the Ysbyty estate in Eryri, for the community. Connection to the outdoors is vital in helping people live healthier lives and by providing new ways to connect with nature. We will create spaces for recreation, contemplation and learning, bridging the gap between people and nature. New walking routes co-created with the community will include local heritage and provide an opportunity to spot curlews, red kites and pied flycatchers in their natural habitat.  

Woodland facilities will offer opportunities for schools and youth groups to encourage the conservationists of tomorrow, and the health of the woodland will be managed by volunteers going forward.  

Mitigating the effects of climate change, National Trust Cymru (NTC) will deliver an ambitious strategy to transform our land, aligning with the outcomes of the National Forest programme.

data.title: #Coed2 Colby Ancient Woodland Enhancement
data.description:
Our vision: - to restore Colby Woodlands to their ancient glory, bringing back a Celtic rainforest!  

The future:- a woodland full of veteran trees, dripping with golden ferns, the air filled with the trill of wood warblers and the black and white flash of pied flycatchers.  

A place of wonder for visitors, with opportunities to reconnect with nature. Where improved footpaths enable new audiences to discover the woodlands and the magic within!  

Returning the woodlands to full health, their ability to sequester carbon, absorb floodwaters and be more resilient to future climate scenarios grows; making an important contribution to climate change mitigation and adaptation.    

The community orchard and new plantings will create spaces for recreation and learning; where the community volunteer, take part and care for their woodland now and into the future - a future where Colby Woodlands takes its place at the heart of the National Forest network.

data.title: Reconnecting the Rooms
data.description:
“For posh people and tourists”. “Intimidating and unwelcome”. “Not for me”. A selection of responses provided by locals about the city’s heritage.

Bath is a place of juxtaposition. Affluent but with a growing inequality gap. Culturally rich but where most communities feel disconnected from heritage. The heritage sector needs to respond as a collective, playing our part to make Bath a more inclusive and fairer city. 

Reconnecting the Rooms aims to use the ethos of Bath Assembly Rooms (BAR) – a place for diverse social assembly – to bring people together to reduce loneliness, improve connection with the city’s heritage, develop skills, and deliver public benefit. 

Our legacy is for BAR to be an ongoing place of 21st century assembly (e.g. queer ballroom dances, music therapy or climate cafes), serving a more diverse audience, celebrating personal heritage and honouring communities from all backgrounds that were, and remain, integral to Bath’s history.

data.title: Keys to the Castle – Unlocking Bodiam’s Past, Present and Future
data.description:
With its moat, drawbridge, towers and castle walls, Bodiam Castle in East Sussex is iconic and picturesque, attracting around 150,000 visitors annually. Bodiam is a gateway to heritage - with many visitors never having been to a heritage site before - but it's not currently fulfilling its amazing potential to inspire, and often disappoints.

We want Bodiam’s fascinating stories and medieval history to spring to life, and for it to play an important role in the local community. 

By using audience-led design we will present Bodiam’s stories through engaging interpretation and hands-on activities - creating an adventure-filled gateway to the world of heritage. 

We will open up more of the castle, making it physically, emotionally and intellectually accessible to all, and enabling visitors to experience the magic of a fairytale castle.

2026 is Bodiam Castle’s National Trust centenary, is the perfect opportunity to celebrate ’the most castle-y castle in England’.

data.title: NT Project 2025
data.description:
Set within the atmospheric Ironbridge Gorge in Shropshire, are a collection of museums, historic sites and structures owned and operated by the Ironbridge Gorge Museum Trust (IGMT).  The birthplace of the Industrial Revolution, this World Heritage Site is an internationally significant and locally loved place that celebrates industrial heritage.  

Increasing financial pressures means that the National Trust (NT) are in discussions about acquiring IGMT’s assets and taking over the operational management of their sites.  This would safeguard IGMT’s built heritage and stories of the Industrial Revolution for future generations to enjoy. 

The NT now needs to complete a feasibility study and due diligence around the asset transfer to prepare a comprehensive business case and operating model.  We are seeking support from the Heritage Fund towards this process, which will run from April to September 2025.

data.title: Reconnecting Scotney
data.description:
Scotney, a me dieval moated castle, mansion and gardens, surrounded by a 780-acre parkland, and hosting one of the UK's best examples of a ‘Picturesque’ landscape, is currently inaccessible, undervalued and not serving its Tunbridge Wells community.

Reconnecting Scotney will: 
•	Improve access to local heritage and green space for those with physical and sensory needs through tactile interpretation, improved paths and a new changing place facility.
•	Preserve significant features of the Grade 1 listed landscape that are at risk of collapse.
•	Protect the environment by creating a 0.6 acre  orchard, climate resilient planting and ‘Garden Guardians’, a schools environmental ambassadors programme.
•	Diversify its audiences by delivering meaningful experiences to address social need, such as ‘Blossom and Breathe: Garden Wellness’ for those experiencing bereavement and loneliness.
•	Strengthen organisational sustainability by improving the visitor experience through a new welcome hub and play area.

One holistic project, three connected solutions: heritage, infrastructure, and community.

data.title: The Nature & Nurture Hub: Arlington
data.description:
Arlington Estate is an important pocket of nature-rich habitat in North Devon, on the doorstep of three of the most disadvantaged communities in Devon. This project will create a new, free, accessible, public Nature & Nurture Hub- a ‘gateway’ into nature for our communities to connect with, enjoy and learn about their distinctive, local natural heritage. 

At the Hub, a packed 18-month programme of tailored activities will break down the barriers that prevent our most marginalised, nature-deprived communities from accessing nature. It will include two bespoke ‘9 Months in Nature’ programmes, an apprenticeship opportunity, a Young Conservationist volunteering project and year-round, ‘entry-level’ nature activities. 

Over two years, 1,000 local people (and 6 partners) will restore 5.3ha of habitat - creating floristically rich meadows and woodland. They will co-create physically and psychologically safe nature spaces, supporting communities to build confidence in nature and deepen their connection with their local natural heritage.

data.title: Midlands Nature Accelerator Project
data.description:
Midland Nature’s long-term vision is of a Midlands region in which nature thrives; air, water and soil are healthy and can adapt to a changing climate; where more people can enjoy access to, and benefit from natural spaces; and where our local economy invests in and benefits from a clean and nature-rich environment. 
The Accelerator Project is the first step in delivering this vision. In these preparatory two years we will work together to develop: 
A foundational set of aggregated landscape-scale nature restoration projects which are ambitious, impactful, publicly accessible and able to attract a variety of funding as “investible propositions”. 
Build relationships with a wide range of natural capital funders. 
Create a financially sustainable new organisation, Midlands Nature, with the capabilities needed to bring all parties together. 
The legacy will be an emergent natural capital market in the Midlands, transforming the viability of nature restoration in the region.

data.title: #COED6 Glan Faenol : Ymestyn Gwreiddiau - Spreading Roots
data.description:
National Trust Cymru’s (NTC) vision is that Glan Faenol is a healthy woodland rich in wildlife, where rare and endemic species thrive, and local people feel welcome and involved.

Despite its picturesque setting on the banks of the Menai Straits, poor or limited access prevents some visitors and communities enjoying the site. This project will create over 1,300 metres of new and improved paths, making it easier and safer to explore and discover the hidden treasures within. 

We will upgrade our workshop space to include tool storage and lighting and an outdoor classroom for local schools. The enhanced facility will help us to recruit more volunteers and enable us to run more woodland skills activities, like woodworking, coppicing and seed collecting. 

Together these enhancements will support Glan Faenol’s aim to become part of the National Forest for Wales  and a place where nature and people grow together.

data.title: #LC Mourne Gullion Landscape Connections
data.description:
The Mourne Gullion Landscape Connections project unites partners, farmers, landowners & communities across 73,294ha in 2 Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty to address the root causes of an iconic landscape under significant pressure. Escalating challenges across the landscape – devastating wildfires, agricultural & land use pollution, uncoordinated land management & growth of recreational use - are contributing to a deepening environmental crisis. 

Through a depth & breadth of quality engagement & collaboration, the project will build on the knowledge and skills among those who live, work and visit this landscape to restore the connection between people and place. It will catalyse the societal, community and individual shifts needed to drive systemic change and support the landscape’s recovery and climate resilience. Modelling best practice, the project will help restore habitats, demonstrate a pathway for sustainable landscape management, enhance accessibility and restore meaningful connections to the rich and diverse natural and cultural heritage.

data.description: This Formally Constituted Organisation Would Use An Award To Celebrate 60 Years Of D-Day By Organising A Number Of Events At Ashridge Estate, Which Provided A Training Area And An Encampment For Troops, As Well As Served As An Emergency Medical Hospital During Ww2.  The Event Would Include: A Reunion Of Veterans With Organised Tours Of The Estate; Archiving Of Memories Collected In A Booklet; A Home Guard Encampment Providing Visual Demonstrations Of Home Guard Training Sessions And Talks On Weapons;  A Battle Re-Enactment By The Living History Association Staging 2 Battles Using Authentic Vehicles And Uniforms.  Other Activities Such As A Military Vehicle Rally And Memorabilia Stalls Will Also Be Available.  A Number Of Schools Have Expressed Interest In Attending And Possibly Contributing To The Activities, As This Would Be An Enhancement To Elements Of The National Curriculum.

People From The Surrounding Villages Will Be Invited To Take Part In A Drama Project To Develop Stories From The 1940s In To A Short Play Portraying Village Life During That Time. data.title: Stoneford Community Garden
data.description: This project will open a 2000m2 green space up to the public for the first time. The project will create a new community garden, connect local people with nature and support green skills development with a diverse engagement and activity programme.

data.title: Civil Society Strengthening Programme-Ghana
data.description: The Civil Society Strengthening Programme (CSSP) aims to strengthen civil society to become more resilient, responsive and effective in delivering the priorities of its constituents. CSSP will strengthen the effectiveness of civil society actors and their advocacy for inclusive participation and access to public services by underserved communities.

data.title: Esso Community Sport for Change Project - Research & Consultation
data.description: This 6 month project will gather factual evidence which will shape future work in Arusha, Tanzania’s second largest city. It is designed to engage the most vulnerable and disadvantaged young people, aged between 15 and 24 years, who live in a slum community. The research will evaluate how sports activities can be used as a vehicle through which these young people can receive support, enabling them to gain access to housing, health and educational services.

data.title: Passage House: Passage to Life Programme
data.description: Physical and emotional abuse, neglect, and being forced into work to support family income are some of the many reasons why children and young people in Brazil leave home to live on the streets. Once on the streets, some turn to drugs, prostitution, and crime and all are at risk of violence and further abuse. This project will support a safe haven for vulnerable children and young people who live and/or work on the streets. Through services such as counselling, provision of basic needs, and access to education/training, children and young people regain their identity and are given a chance to begin again. Prevention and family outreach activities raise community awareness of the issues and advocate for the rights, safety and health of children and young people. As a result of the work, young people will get the support they need to be reunified with their families and communities, and learn skills to gain economically viable alternatives to a life on the streets.

data.title: The time is now: PLHIV claiming our rights!
data.description: 65,350 people living with HIV and AIDS will benefit from a comprehensive approach for securing health and rights. The project will expand a successful effort funded by Comic Relief and add new technical aspects. Partners will increase the project’s reach from 7 to 10 districts in five Zimbabwean provinces. This will increase access to services, help to secure livelihoods, reduce discrimination in communities, provide legal assistance in specific cases, and seek improvements in policy and laws. New focus areas include access to HIV treatment for children, reducing self-stigma among people living with HIV and AIDS, and increasing male involvement for prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission.

data.title: From Exploitation to Education and Empowerment through Child Friendly Communities
data.description: Children in the rural areas of Uganda and Malawi are often forced to work on farms as agricultural labourers from a young age. This not only puts them at risk of harm from dangerous equipment and pesticides, it also prevents them from attending school and can have lifelong damaging consequences. This project will work with communities to ensure that children are sent to school instead of being forced to work in the fields. The result will be children who are better protected from the dangers of work; and who have the chance to acquire an education and have a better start in life.

data.title: Empowering women in Kordofan through non-wood forest products for income and food security
data.description: Women in central Sudan harvest forest products for income and food but stay poor, as men retain most of the income, and because collection and marketing are unorganized. This project will create 15 women-led associations to collect, store, process and market wild fruits, gum Arabica and honey, and to share learning with 36 other villages. Participatory community agreements on natural resource use will be made. A small grants fund will help individual micro-business to start- up. A revolving loan fund will promote alternatives to firewood and charcoal for cooking, reducing deforestation. Women will achieve 40% higher earnings. 2,242 association members, women taking loans and micro-businesses will benefit.

data.title: Financial inclusion for HIV positive people facing discrimination in Mozambique
data.description: In Mozambique about 1.6 million people are living with HIV. Some feel guilty or too ashamed to acknowledge their positive status for fear of rejection, refusing to seek treatment or counselling; others try to access economic opportunities and services but face stigma and discrimination. This can lead people and their families into a cycle of low incomes, poor nutrition, ill health, inability to work, and falling income.This project aims to break this cycle of poverty by supporting thousands of people with HIV to access the financial resources they need to improve livelihoods and demand policies which enable them to live a full and equal life.

data.title: Building entrepreneurship for water, liquid, and solid waste management in slums of Dar es Salaam
data.description: The majority of Dar es Salaam’s population live in slums with inadequate access to water, toilets and garbage disposal services. As a result many people are vulnerable to diseases such as cholera. Temeke Municipality wants to improve these conditions and has asked WaterAid to support existing small businesses to provide some of the required services. Enterprises will be helped to develop business skills and to use improved techniques so that they can provide water, empty pit latrines safely and operate basic garbage collection services on a profitable basis. New garbage collection points and facilities for safely processing the sludge from latrines will make conditions safer for everyone.

data.title: Safe cities: improving safety, mobility and public services for vulnerable women and girls in DRC
data.description: Cities can be threatening and violent places the world over – and for women this is especially true. In the DRC, a country with a long recent history of war, where violence is part of life, things are worse. And for women market gardeners and street vendors who travel early or after dark, the risks of sexual and physical violence, robbery and theft are extreme.This project will work in communities to change underlying attitudes; build skills and confidence of women; and persuade groups like the police and local authorities to make practical changes – leading to long term change. As one of 14 projects in an international ‘Safer Cities’ initiative the project will share learning and ideas widely.

data.title: Improving WASH in the slums of Addis Ababa
data.description: The slums of Ethiopia's capital city, Addis Ababa are very congested. Rubbish is rarely collected, and there are few proper toilets. Many people, especially children have diarrhoea.This project plans to train health workers and volunteers, and construct communal toilets and showers. They will be run by local people who will charge small fees to people who use them. Women who collect and recycle waste as a business will also be trained and given proper equipment.As a result the overall environment in these slums should improve; people will become healthier, and some of the poorest slum dwellers will be able to increase their incomes.

data.title: Children and young people at risk: building resilience- from research to practice
data.description: Crime and violence are major problems in South Africa's Eastern Cape, particularly for youngsters who are often the victims as well as the perpetrators.This project equips young people and their families with the skills they need to resist violence. Schools will be assisted to become safer places, and to better understand how to help young people avoid becoming casualties of violence and from becoming involved in violence.Providing the government with strong evidence of what works will help make the prevention of violence a priority, while practical training to teachers, social workers and others will improve their care and support of young people.

recipientOrganization.name: Centre for Justice and Crime Prevention (CJCP)

data.title: Improving the quality of pre-primary education in Ghana through a network Model Practice Classrooms.
data.description: The Fast-track Transformational Teacher Training (FTTT) programme is a direct recommendation of the Ghana Education Services (GES). The programme links in-service teachers with pre-service student teachers, & places them together for 1 year in a model classroom environment. The training approach is intensive & combines practical workshops with in-classroom coaching. The FTTT is recognised as the highest priority activity being undertaken by GES to implement the Kindergarten Operational Plan. Sabre Charitable Trust (SCT) is GES’ lead implementing partner for the FTTT, providing funding & programme management expertise to GES & the College of Education in delivering the FTTT. This works to find a scalable solution.

data.title: Kibera Fund II - Enhancing Secure Livelihoods for Slum Residents
data.description: Kibera, on the edge of Nairobi, is the largest slum in Africa, with over a million people living in crowded conditions. Few people are in school or have regular jobs.This grant will enable a well-respected Kenyan grant-making foundation to support local organisations based in Kibera with funds, training and advice, with a particular emphasis on youth, women and sustainability. These organisations will be encouraged to become self-supporting so that they can raise funding from other local donors and implement a wide variety of activities to help some of the poorest people improve their lives.In addition, the grant will facilitate some of Comic Relief's communications work in Kibera.

data.title: To improve the quality of life of street vendors and marketers living and working in slums in Kenya
data.description: In Kenya most traders buy and sell in the street. This means constantly moving, or struggling to claim and keep their patch. Toilets and water are a rarity. By coming together and demanding recognition and basic facilities in return for the fees they pay, a national group is starting to change things.This project will help increase membership of the group and ensure that the police and council officials understand what traders are allowed to do. It will also negotiate for traders to receive loans and train them in business skills. As their lives become more stable they will be able to increase earnings and improve their working conditions.

data.title: END AIDS portal: Scaling-up HIV and AIDS support services in Zambia through SMS
data.description: New HIV treatment guidelines in Zambia are not well understood by people living with HIV or by clinicians, and treatment centres are increasingly understaffed. Poor adherence to therapy increases drug resistance and ultimately the number of AIDS-related deaths.This project will use mobile phone technology to improve access to information and support about HIV treatment in Lusaka province. Text messages can be sent to health agents, and bulk messages will widely disseminate health information.This innovative project will contribute to the goal of reducing the number of new HIV infections to zero.

data.title: Extension of the Betteh Tumara Freetown Vocational Training project
data.description: 60% of young people in Sierra Leone are unemployed or underemployed. Many had their education disrupted by civil war. Lack of appropriate skills in the labour force slows the country's development. High quality, affordable vocational training in Freetown is not readily available.The project will train young men and women in life skills and vocational courses matched to employer demand. It will offer business training and mentorship to young entrepreneurs, facilitate work placements and employment through outreach to companies, and raise revenue by charging firms for recruitment and in-house employee training. Of 990 people trained, 514 will secure a job, improve their jobs or establish a business.

data.title: Empowering communities to collectively abandon FGM/C in Somaliland
data.description: A draft policy on female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) was drawn up in 2012 as part of the National Gender Policy in Somaliland. These documents rest with the Ministry of Religious Affairs as there has been relative difficulty in gaining public support for them amongst influential religious leaders.With 99% prevalence of FGM/C in the country, this project aims to support Women's Coalitions & School based Youth Groups to raise awareness of FGM/C issues as part of a wider women's rights framework. The work will be linked at a national & regional level through coordination of a sector specific network, support to regional and national ministerial officers, and the production of research which can be used for lobbying.

data.title: Connecting Communities:Learning for Life
data.description: A quarter of 15-24 year-olds in Zambia have never been to school. Many orphans, especially girls, don’t finish basic education or go to high school. This project trains committees to identify 14-16 year-olds not in school and those who may drop out. Some of the vulnerable young people work with the committees to set up clubs that provide business skills, homework help, drama and sports activities. Together, they lobby for better government services. The neediest families get help with school fees, materials and are supported to develop initiatives for them to earn money. As a result and with the support of parents and the wider community more young people finish school. They and their families have more chance of work.

recipientOrganization.name: The Cecily Eastwood Zambian AIDS Orphans Appeal

data.title: Improving Life Chances&Household Income of People with Disabilities in 8 Subcounties-Northern Uganda
data.description: There are about 16,000 people with disabilities in Moyo District, N. Uganda needing specific assistance to have a chance of getting a job or setting up a new enterprise in a rural area recovering from a long period of armed conflict.This project will start to work with 1,000 people with disabilities to provide rehabilitation support, training, career counselling, and acquire locally relevant vocational skills. Some 600 will get group support, loans, or intensive training to take up formal jobs or set up new businesses for themselves. Traditional attitudes to disability are harsh however, so there will be outreach and awareness raising to reduce barriers and social stigma and find partners.

data.title: Amplifying the voices of people affected by HIV in Zimbabwe
data.description: HIV remains a critical health threat in Zimbabwe where 1.4 million adults and 170,000 children under 14 live with HIV. Progressio and four Zimbabwean partners will extend a successful project to reach specific populations for prevention, care and access to treatment. The project will reach almost 18,000 beneficiaries including prisoners, truck drivers and other employees of the transport industry, and people working in the informal sector and in small and medium enterprises. Advocacy will also play an important role to ensure implementation of legally required HIV workplace policies, increase children’s access to HIV treatment, and protect the rights and health of prison inmates.

data.title: iCCM +: Access to quality health services for childhood diseases and MNC in 14 districts of Uganda
data.description: Children under 5 in Midwest Uganda are dying shortly after birth or in early childhood from pneumonia, malaria, and diarrhoea often because their illness is not appropriately diagnosed or treated in time. Women face complications in pregnancy or childbirth sometimes because they do not go to antenatal care early enough or do not deliver in health facilities. This project will train and support Village Health Teams to provide emergency treatment for the key childhood illnesses at village level, to use rapid diagnosis tests for malaria, to promote healthy maternal newborn and childcare practices at home, and to encourage women to take up antenatal care, skilled birth attendance, and postnatal care. There will be nearly 1.5m beneficiaries.

data.title: Developing the FTO cashew supply chain in West Africa for producers, workers, SMEs & the environment
data.description: Certified fruits and nuts are an important source of income for thousands of farmers in Burkina Faso and neighbouring countries, also creating steady jobs in transport, distribution, and processing for hundreds of workers, mostly women, in small enterprises and cooperatives.Fullwell Mill and Gebana are two social enterprises with a vision of helping more than 2,000 of these farmers and entrepreneurs to move up the value chain. The project will help them to plant more cashew trees, improve farming and yields, do more primary processing, reduce costs and earn more, whatever their role.The project will also test alternative cashew products and how to make safe energy from cashew nut waste.

data.title: Speak Up 2
data.description: Over 20 years of conflict and poverty left 77% of adults (84% of females) in South Sudan non-literate. Many of these are returnees and internally displaced people. Increasing English literacy is vital, as it is now the official language for all education and business. This project will apply REFLECT adult literacy methods to English teaching in South Sudan. It follows a successful previous project but now includes non-literate learners. Each of two 18 month courses will comprise twelve months' group literacy work, followed by six months' aural practice using radio and pod cast interactive lessons. Its method emphasizes self-empowerment and inclusivity, building trust and self-confidence.

data.title: Our Bodies, Our Lives: ensuring women’s access to quality anti-retrovirals in Malawi.
data.description: Antiretroviral drugs (ARVs) save the lives of people with HIV, but can have disfiguring effects on some women’s bodies. Changes in body shape can cause distress, and real or perceived stigma and discrimination, leading some women to stop taking ARVs. This has provided a spark for women living with HIV in Malawi to demand drugs with fewer side effects.This project will help HIV positive women learn more about HIV treatment, their own well-being, and their rights to HIV and other services. Working with women across Malawi, the project aims to improve women’s access to ARVs and address stigma, discrimination and other barriers that limit access to HIV treatment and health and social care.

data.title: Protecting the rights of street connected children and young people in Nairobi
data.description: Children and young people living and working in the rubbish dumps and slums of Nairobi are in an extremely hazardous situation, facing violence, abuse, trauma, and bereavement as part of their daily lives. This project will work intensively with children in such situations, it will provide those who are worst off with a roof over their heads, it will give them treatment to recover and offer them opportunities to acquire an education and skills. It will support parents, communities and schools to better protect children themselves. Vulnerable children will have greater physical and emotional security and enjoy a more positive future alongside their families and communities.

data.title: Small scale business development and community mobilisation for healthy and clean urban slums
data.description: In the crowded slums of Malawi's two major cities, Lilongwe and Blantyre, water has to be stored in people's homes and easily gets contaminated. Few people have access to toilets and many of these overflow as there is no emptying system in place. Also solid waste is rarely collected.This project will enable local community groups to take on contracts to empty toilets. They will also run publicity campaigns to make people more aware of the health risks of contaminated water. Water filters and latrines will be sold at low prices, and local people will be assisted to start up their own businesses to collect, recycle, and sell waste: the compost will then be used for producing flowers and vegetables.

data.title: Protecting and rehabilitating vulnerable ‘at risk’ young people in Togo
data.description: Hundreds of young people, many of them street children, are detained in Togo’s prisons. They are wrongfully detained, often for long periods, by a flawed justice system. All have difficult backgrounds, poor prospects, and are prone to violence by the police, prison staff and other detainees. Based on previous tried and tested work, this project will work with young detainees for a fair hearing and with officials to end the abuse of youths who are arrested. Released youth and those at risk of getting into trouble will be helped to reconnect with their families, be accepted into their communities, and earn a decent living, breaking the cycle of re-offending.

data.title: Securing forest community livelihoods through sustainable smallholder cocoa development
data.description: While world cocoa prices are rising cocoa farmers living on the edge of the Gola rainforest in Sierra Leone are leaving their farms and adopting farming practices which drive deforestation to feed their families.As a result of the civil war farmers can't access the information, training and inputs they need leading to lower yields, a reputation for poor quality and prices significantly below the market rate resulting in reduced incomes.Using a tried and tested approach this project aims to build the capacity of local partners to provide services which increase productivity and quality; build a strong producer organization; and establish a Gola cocoa brand in the international market.

data.title: Strengthening Healthcare Delivery in Iyolwa Sub-county of Tororo District, Uganda
data.description: Uganda has high child and maternal mortality rates. In some parts of Uganda, access to good quality maternal and child health care is poor. Iyolwa Health Centre, in eastern Uganda, was a run-down clinic that was refurbished as part of the documentary 'Operation Health for Comic Relief' for Red Nose Day 2015. This project will sustain the gains made during the investment in the physical infrastructure of the clinic, and will ensure that high quality care will be provided, through district leadership. Health workers will be trained to provide better care, and the community will be engaged to hold the service providers to account. The whole community of Iyolwa sub-county will get the health care they need.

data.title: GAVI RND15
data.description: The Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI) increases access to childhood immunisation, including new and underused vaccines. Comic Relief is supporting the delivery of a combination of vaccines in several low-income countries. These include vaccines that protect against pneumococcal disease, one of the leading causes of childhood pneumonia, and rotavirus, the lead cause of severe diarrhoea among infants and young children. Together, pneumonia and diarrhoea cause 30% of global deaths of children under five. As well, children will be vaccinated against other potentially lethal infections: diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, hepatitis B, and Hib bacterial infection which causes meningitis and pneumonia.

data.title: GFATM RND15
data.description: This funding will be used by the Global Fund for the purchase of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT) medications, for the purchase of long lasting insecticide treated nets (LLINs) and for the strengthening of health system capacity in Africa.

recipientOrganization.name: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

data.title: Primary and secondary education needs assessment in Gedo region of Somalia
data.description: A detailed education needs assessment will be undertaken in the Gedo region of Somalia. This is 2nd largest region in the country with a population made up of nomadic & pastoralist communities. Somalia has one of the lowest enrolment rates in education with only 42% children in school. Low numbers of qualified teachers, in particular female teachers, exacerbate the challenges in education provision. Very little education provision is available across all 7 districts in the region.The needs assessment will understand the current situation of primary & secondary schools, the physical state of schools, rationale for drop out & non-attendance, the quality of education & ways to improve provision.

data.title: Ipaja Special Needs Social Enterprise & Empowerment Project
data.description: Some disabled children in Nigeria go to special units in primary schools. Sadly there are not enough to meet the need and there is no support for the children on their parents when school finishes.This project will pilot ideas to prepare them for life in back in the community. Training facilities will be provided within a special unit to teach skills for work such as shoe making and tailoring. And apprenticeships will be negotiated within the community for them to learn skills. Additional support will be provided to ensure that the products are marketed and sold to ensure profit.The project will be carefully monitored with a view to replicating it in other units and schools.

data.title: Wamba Girls' Education Project Consultation
data.description: Half the girls in Samburu Kenya do not reach the end of primary school. Families live nomadic lives, dependent on livestock. Parents prioritise boys’ education so only a third of those who pass the final primary exams are girls. This research enables girls, boys, families, communities and government to come together to analyse the barriers to girls’ education. They make video stories of the community history and plan for the future, making sure women’s and girls’ views are heard. They assess what gaps in the school system need tackling. As a result, they will design a project to help girls stay in and do better in education and that gives women more influence in school management.

data.title: Developing an Inhalant Rehabilitation Programme for Street Connected Young People in Uganda
data.description: Drug addiction is a major problem amongst the 8000 children living on the streets in Uganda and is a barrier to them accessing services and leaving the streets. The main drug used on the streets is Mafuta (aeroplane fuel) which is inhaled through the mouth. Mafuta is cheaper to buy than food, and is readily available in urban settings. However it seriously impairs children's health, is highly addictive, and can be lethal.This research builds on previous research into global best practice in rehabilitation and cure. It will form the basis for a major new intervention to provide holistic care and support for young people trying to get off Mafuta. It will also add to global knowledge of it.

recipientOrganization.name: Support and Love Via Education International

data.title: Investigating and designing solutions to maternal, newborn and child health challenges in Oyam District, Uganda
data.description: Women and babies in northern Uganda suffer very poor health and many die during pregnancy and childbirth. Oyam district is still recovering from 20 years of conflict and ruined health services. The partner, CUAMM, has worked there since 2007 rebuilding health centres and strengthening service delivery. Although increasing numbers of women are now using health services, many more are left behind. CUAMM has asked WCF for help to reach out into villages using their successful approach of mobilising women's groups.This grant is for an 11-day consultation with women, men, local leaders, Ministry of Health and health workers. The information collected will be used for a full project proposal.

data.title: End Child, Early and Forced marriage for girls in Katsina State, Nigeria
data.description: In rural Northern Nigeria almost half of all girls are married to older men, usually against their will, by the age of 15. These girls then have to leave school early, and they face a variety of health hazards, especially in relation to childbirth.This grant will allow a well-established local NGO to undertake research on this issue, including extensive consultations with women themselves, and local leaders. This research will then be used to help prepare a detailed proposal which will focus on the best ways of tackling this problem.

recipientOrganization.name: Pan African Development Education Advocacy Programme

data.title: Green-growth income initiatives for forest people
data.description: The proposal will result in a research report informing a proposed new initiative around Metemma forest, Ethiopia. The objective of the initiative is to increase incomes, stabilize livelihoods & generate employment for the poorest rural & forest-dependent communities in this area. The initiative will promote & professionalize the production, processing, enterprise & market development of non-timber forest products (NTFPs) - gum, resin and incense. Surnarma & SET have significant experience of similar work (community based forest management delivering both conservation & poverty reduction goals) & have been invited to work in Metemma because of their previous success elsewhere.

data.title: Reaching the most vulnerable children in the Dominican Republic
data.description: Many children in Dominican Republic face harsh and dangerous lives. Children working on the street are at risk of all kinds of abuse. Child marriage and teenage pregnancy is extremely high. Migrant families, many of which are from Haiti, are often deemed illegal so parents cannot officially work and children cannot attend formal schools. As a result, sex work, drug trafficking and unemployment are soaring and a lot of families are affected by HIV and AIDS.The proposed approach is to give grants to small local organisations to help them become more effective by learning from each other to bring lasting change for the children and families they work with. Additionally, there will be support for families of children at risk by providing medical care and counselling; children will be taught the skills to survive and projects funded will provide educational support such access to schooling and help with after school homework.As a result, children stop harmful work and are better protected from HIV and early pregnancy and have improved education and skills.

recipientOrganization.name: The Global Fund for Children UK Trust

data.title: Waves for Change: Surf Therapy for Communities of High Violence
data.description: Young people (YP) in South African townships are exposed to high levels of violence, neglect, HIV and poverty. An estimated 20% of YP have post traumatic stress disorder and they face increased risk of school drop-out, unemployment and exclusion from society.Through this project YP will participate in regular 'surf therapy' sessions, their primary care-givers (parents or guardians) and teachers will receive support to identify symptoms of trauma and engage with YP, and older youth will undergo training to become qualified Youth Care Workers.As a result, YP will demonstrate improved emotional health, school attendance and vocational opportunities, and reduced anti-social behaviour.

data.title: Let’s Coach and Let’s Lead
data.description: There are high levels of poverty, crime, HIV, and youth unemployment in the townships of the Tshwane District of South Africa. Adolescent girls and young women are a particularly vulnerable group, experiencing high levels of gender based violence, including rape.This project uses sport as an entry point to provide a safe space for engagement with girls, and also as a way of engaging with the wider community about rights, violence, and sexual and reproductive health. Young women will be trained as leaders to deliver the activities in primary schools.This will improve the ability of girls and young women to influence decisions that impact their lives and facilitate access to services.

data.title: Combining B&MA with pyscho-social services to support at-risk young people in inner-city JHB
data.description: In South Africa more than fifty percent of all teenagers will know someone who has died violently. 19% are orphans (one or both parents have died), 25% do not live with parents, 60% live in poverty, and homicide rates, already 6 times the global average, increase with age between 10 – 14 yrs.This project seeks to tackle these statistics by supporting alienated young people through a boxing and martial arts teaching programme linked to intensive personal development support and career mentoring.The global network of Fight for Peace will support a local group which has exceptional success already in this field to grow in strength and reach out more effectively to both boys and girls.

data.title: Enabling South African Youth through Skateboarding and Education
data.description: In Johannesburg, youth from low income and migrant backgrounds face violence, lack of opportunities, and social isolation. Education quality is often poor and due to a lack of basic skills, such as literacy, numeracy and problem-solving, youth unemployment is also high (31.5%).After extensive research, Skateistan will run an after-school and out-of-school program and engage with at-risk youth through the use of skateboarding teaching and competitions, linked to arts based learning.It will also address the issue of gender based violence and intimidation of young girls through single sex sessions and female only teaching periods, along with arts activities and future life skills mentoring.

data.title: Smallholder Market Access
data.description: More than half of all Zambians rely on agriculture for income. Few small-scale farmers have a concrete basis on which to decide what to grow, when and who to sell to and what the prices are for the crops they know how to produce. IDE has tested a simple buyer-seller system which, with a basic telephone, gets information and trading contacts into the hands of farmers. The project will start a social enterprise to build up from 6,000 farmers registered so far to 40,000 in four regions, developing more of the services and products that farmers and traders say they need to make trading more efficient, less risky and ensure take-home earnings for both parties rise and household poverty is reduced

data.title: Strengthening m2m systems for improved retention of mother-baby-pairs in PMTCT care and treatment.
data.description: Every day in sub-Saharan Africa, nearly 600 children get HIV from their mothers. Effective methods are available to keep HIV-positive mothers and their babies healthy. For various reasons many HIV-positive women don’t take up the recommended treatment and care services to prevent passing HIV to their child.This project will deploy an electronic system that will help track mother-baby pairs in six countries. Clients will be followed up by peer mentor mothers, who will encourage women to get the care they need to live well with HIV, avoid passing it to their child, and take their child to HIV testing and care services.

data.title: Strengthening the Yanfolila Mutual Health Insurance Scheme and reducing risks to women’s health
data.description: Health care is not free in Mali and poor people in rural areas either have to pay exorbitant fees for basic health services and medicines, or go without. The Government started a nationwide community health insurance scheme in 2008 but the subsequent financial crisis and political unrest prevented it from taking off beyond a few pilots.This project will build on tested savings and credit work with women’s groups in Yanfolila commune to expand health insurance. About 2,000 women will benefit from health promotion sessions and they and their families (6,680 new members across 35 villages) will be able to afford health services. Lives will be saved. Lessons will be shared across Mali.

data.title: Accelerated Access to Finance and Markets for Women and Young Farmers
data.description: Many small-scale farmers are in desperate conditions in Zambia. The poorest households are often malnourished and trapped in unpredictable, subsistence farming.The aim here is to smooth the entry of 7,500 determined and hard-working women and young farmers, from subsistence into more effective production methods, including their first access to credit. A new Guarantee Fund run by ZNFU will partially back their bank applications to buy good seeds and inputs. With technical training they will now have a shot at forming marketing groups, growing enough to eat and a surplus to sell, and regularly earning more cash for savings and family needs.

data.title: Bangladesh Firestarter Initiative (BFI)
data.description: Action Aid will act as a devolved small grant maker for the Bangladesh Firestarter Initiative, a reactive small grants scheme. The Initiative will provide small grants (under £10k) to emerging/ innovative youth-led organisations/clubs leading advocacy projects outside Dhaka. Specifically targeting young women, girls & minority communities, the scope of the funding will be to: - build capacity - provide peer–to-peer learning/ sharing opportunities - provide mentorship & coaching.The Initiative will help youth-led organisations/clubs to establish linkages with the wider youth sector in Bangladesh, including with potential donors, thereby encouraging the sustainability of the funded projects beyond the Firestarter grant term.

data.title: Completing the cycle for children on the streets: outreach - engagement - reintegration - prevention
data.description: Life on the streets can be very harsh for street children, especially girls, and the risk of violence and abuse is a feature of daily life. This project uses surfing as a way to engage street children in Durban, helping them leave the streets, receive physical and emotional care and learn new skills to prepare them for the future. Wherever possible, street children are supported to return to their families and communities. Work will also be done to, where possible, prevent at-risk children leaving home and making a life on the streets. The project results should be children living in more stable environments, improved confidence and well-being.

data.title: Leave no child behind: Improving Early Childhood Development in Malawi
data.description: Children with disability are often hidden away from public life and rarely participate in education. Families face numerous barriers ranging from general misunderstanding, lack of knowledge, lack of teacher capacity, inappropriate school environment leading to very poor access to education. Sightsavers will work with several local & international partners in Malawi to provide a holistic approach to supporting families to enrol their children in early childhood education by supporting the quality of inclusive education offered, improving links to primary schools and improving retention throughout the education system. By working with schools, communities and government the project will offer an affordable model for future.

recipientOrganization.name: Royal Commonwealth Society for the Blind

data.title: Youth@Work
data.description: Youth@Work is the only national initiative for unemployed youth and early school leavers; providing training and employment opportunities for young people in Honiara and in selected provinces. Young people take part in an innovative vocational training and employability training programme, or are supported to set up and run their own businesses and can take part in a youth-run ‘Youth Market’ in the centre of Honiara to promote youth-led social enterprises. They will include all young people released from prison in their programme as well as a specific component to integrate disabled young people.
